children: is already making major post-merger moves. The media giant announced that it will combine Warner Bros. Television and Paramount Television Studios into a single TV studio entity that will have more than 100 productions under its control. The new organization will be called Warner Bros. Television Studios and will launch early next year.

The merged studio unit is being co-led by Channing Dungey (head of Warner Bros. Television Group) and Matt Thunell (president of Paramount Television Studios). Both will report to George Cheeks, who oversees Skydance's
As part of the same broader TV restructuring, Skydance

has also folded its television animation assets (Warner Bros. Animation, Cartoon Network Studios, Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe, and Nickelodeon Animation Studios) into a single division called Skydance Television Animation.
The consolidation is a major piece of Skydance's
post-merger integration strategy aimed at achieving $6B in annual synergies within three years. Separately, Skydance
is considering combining Paramount+ and HBO Max into one streaming service.
